adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission logic uses && where || is required in isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying team admins who are not owners
Blacklist email comparison is case-mismatched since env list is lowercased but guest is compared as-is, allowing blocklist bypass
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same flaw: the blacklist/env list is lowercased while the guest email is compared without normalization, enabling bypass via uppercase characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive existing-attendee dedup allows duplicate attendees for mixed-case emails

adjudication.rationale: The new guest-dedup logic is case-sensitive. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees with `guest === attendee.email` and checks blacklist with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`; neither normalizes case. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` also uses `new Set(emails)` which is case-sensitive. This allows adding duplicates like `User@Example.com` when `user@example.com` already exists, creating duplicate attendees differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx imports from its own package barrel @calcom/ui, creating a circular dependency risk

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from the package barrel `@calcom/ui`. But `packages/ui/index.tsx` (the same barrel) now exports `MultiEmail` via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, which dynamically imports `./MultiEmail`. This creates a self-referential import path (`MultiEmail.tsx` -> `@calcom/ui` -> `MultiEmailLazy` -> `MultiEmail.tsx`), a circular dependency risk introduced by the diff. It may or may not break at runtime depending on bundling/module resolution, but it’s a concrete architecture issue grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with ctx.user (the caller) instead of the booking's organizer, so calendar updates fail or use wrong credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permission checks allow non-organizers (e.g., an attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...)` and `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`). But the calendar update uses credentials from the caller: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. If the caller is an attendee/team member rather than `booking.userId` (the organizer), this will use the wrong credentials and can fail to update the organizer’s connected calendars or update the wrong account. The diff even loads `booking.user.credentials` but never uses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog initializes multiEmailValue to [""] instead of [], making the empty-string guard dead code and the empty UI state unreachable
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the component initializes the multi-email value with an array containing an empty string ("[""]") rather than an empty array ([]), which breaks/blocks proper empty-state handling and makes related empty/validation logic ineffective. The candidate explicitly calls out the incorrect initialization and its consequences, aligning with the golden suggestion to start with [] and handle empty state in the MultiEmail component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail with a CONFIRMED REQUEST ICS for a booking they never accepted, and it may not be imported in email-manager.ts, risking compile failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sendAddGuestsEmails` intentionally sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to attendees whose email is in `newGuests` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` to the others. Whether sending a CONFIRMED/REQUEST ICS to newly-added guests is “wrong” is a product/behavior assumption not verifiable from the diff alone. Also, the claim that it “may not be imported in email-manager.ts” isn’t supported by the shown diff: the new templates are imported (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`), and the diff doesn’t establish that `AttendeeScheduledEmail` is missing (it may already be imported elsewhere in the file outside the shown context).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses AND instead of OR for team admin/owner in addGuests.handler.ts, so only users with both roles pass and non-team bookings block everyone

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning only users who are both admin and owner pass the team-role branch. That is an overly restrictive permission check and likely unintended (the variable name implies OR). However, the finding’s claim that “non-team bookings block everyone” isn’t supported: non-team bookings can still be modified by the organizer (`booking.userId === user.id`) or an attendee (`booking.attendees` contains `user.email`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with raw guests list instead of uniqueGuests, bypassing deduplication/blacklist filtering and causing mislabeled notification emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters/derives `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees + blacklisted emails) and only creates new attendee records from `uniqueGuests`, but later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` input. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the `newGuests` list to decide which email template to send per attendee (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), so passing the raw list can misclassify existing attendees (e.g., if the caller included an already-attending email, it will be filtered out from DB insert but still present in `guests`, causing that attendee to be treated as a “new guest” for notification purposes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-state or time check allows guests to be added to cancelled or past bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`) updates `booking.attendees` for any booking ID the caller has permission for, without checking any booking state (e.g., cancelled) or temporal constraints (e.g., `booking.startTime` already in the past). The handler fetches `startTime/endTime` but never compares them to `dayjs()`/now, and it also doesn’t query/check a `status`/`cancelled` field before performing `prisma.booking.update(...)`, so guests can be added to historical (and potentially cancelled) bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seats-based bookings lack a seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check, allowing guest count to exceed the seats limit

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`) appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` based only on uniqueness/blacklist filtering, and never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count) before adding. Since the feature is exposed from `BookingListItem` for bookings generally, this can allow adding guests beyond a seats-based capacity limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests present in the diff for the addGuests mutation, schema, permission logic, or sendAddGuestsEmails

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (new `addGuests` TRPC mutation in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx`, handler with permission checks and DB updates in `addGuests.handler.ts`, new schema `addGuests.schema.ts`, and new email sending logic `sendAddGuestsEmails` plus new templates). No test files are added or modified in the diff to cover this mutation, permission logic, attendee updates, or the new email-sending behavior, so the finding is accurate and is a concrete review concern rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty-input case in AddGuestsDialog handleAdd silently does nothing with no error feedback, leaving the dialog open with a seemingly broken button

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd`, the empty-input case is handled by `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` with no toast/error state and without closing the dialog. `MultiEmail` allows removing all fields (it splices the array on remove), so `multiEmailValue` can become `[]`, making the Add button appear to do nothing and leaving the dialog open with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing translation keys add_another and emailed_you_and_any_other_attendees in en/common.json, risking raw keys or empty strings in emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new translation lookups for `t("add_another")` (in `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`) and `this.t("emailed_you_and_any_other_attendees")` (in the new email templates’ ICS subtitle). However, the PR diff does not show the full contents of `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`, only a few hunks. From this diff alone we cannot verify that those keys are missing from `en/common.json` (they may already exist elsewhere in the file or in another namespace). لذلك the claim that they are missing is not provably true from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuests handler is add-only with no remove-guest or edit-guest path, so a mistyped email permanently pollutes the attendee list and triggers irreversible calendar/email side effects

adjudication.rationale: The new mutation `addGuestsHandler` only ever appends attendees (`prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` in `addGuests.handler.ts`) and then triggers side effects (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`). This PR does not introduce any corresponding remove/edit flow in the UI or API, so correcting a mistyped email is not addressed within this change and could be a product/UX gap given the calendar/email updates. However, the claim that it is "permanent" cannot be verified from the diff because a separate remove/edit endpoint could exist elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires user to be BOTH admin AND owner, making the team-admin authorization path dead code for admins who are not the owner

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with an `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the flag is only true if the user is *both* a team admin and the team owner. This causes team admins who are not the owner to fail the authorization check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ... FORBIDDEN`), making the intended “admin” authorization path ineffective for non-owner admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee (guest, not organizer) passes the permission check and can trigger calendar updates and email sends against the organizer's booking, an unintended write capability exposed to external attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission gate explicitly allows any authenticated user who is an existing attendee on the booking to proceed: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. That means a non-organizer attendee can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, which performs a DB write (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), updates the organizer’s calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and triggers emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. This is an unintended write capability if attendees are meant to be read-only participants. (Additionally, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, which likely mis-implements the intended admin/owner check.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: New generic MultiEmail form primitive added and publicly exported from the shared @calcom/ui package with no requirement traceability and no other consumer (scope drift)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new `MultiEmail` primitive is immediately consumed by the new `AddGuestsDialog` (`import { ... MultiEmail ... } from "@calcom/ui";` in `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`). So the claim that it has “no other consumer” is false based on this PR. “No requirement traceability” is also not something verifiable from the diff alone, and “scope drift” is a subjective process concern rather than a concrete diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendee records are created with name: "" with no reconciliation against existing users or enforcement of seatsPerTimeSlot, so adding guests can exceed the event's seat capacity with no error

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are unconditionally appended via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (the capacity field is only copied into the `evt` object later). This means a booking for a seated event can have more attendees added than the configured seat limit, with no error or prevention. The "name: \"\"" part is also true (`guestsFullDetails` sets `name: ""`), but the verifiable correctness issue introduced by this diff is the missing seat-capacity enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both admin and owner rather than either

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and typical authorization semantics, this likely should be `||` so either role can authorize adding guests; as written, legitimate admins (not owners) or owners (not admins) would be denied unless they also satisfy `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email duplicate check in guest dedupe is case-sensitive, producing duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduping uses strict equality against existing attendee emails (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`) and against the blacklist (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., lowercased), adding `Foo@Example.com` when `foo@example.com` already exists will bypass the check and can create a duplicate attendee row. The client-side uniqueness refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` also uses a case-sensitive `Set`, reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests can be added to cancelled/declined bookings due to missing status filter/guard, triggering emails and calendar updates for non-existent events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches a booking by `id` only (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and then unconditionally updates attendees, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with no check/guard on any booking status/state. The diff also adds the UI action unconditionally in `BookingListItem` (no status-based gating). While the diff does not show the booking status fields or the app’s rules for cancelled/declined bookings, the lack of any state validation is a concrete, diff-grounded gap that could allow adding guests (and triggering calendar/email side effects) for bookings that should be immutable (e.g., cancelled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive incorrect scheduled-confirmation emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler correctly computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted) and only adds those (`createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }`). However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array, not `uniqueGuests`. In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing raw `guests` means an existing attendee email included in the request would be treated as a "new guest" and receive the scheduled/confirmation email incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking fetched with findFirst and no scoping, with hand-rolled permission logic that can diverge from the rest of the router's query scoping (including exact string email comparison for isAttendee)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the booking is retrieved via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` with no additional scoping tied to `ctx.user`, and authorization is enforced later via custom logic (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isOrganizer`, `isAttendee`). This creates a maintainability/consistency risk vs. router-level scoping patterns elsewhere (not shown here) because access control is “hand-rolled” per-handler. The finding’s note about exact string email comparison is also grounded: `isAttendee` is computed with `attendee.email === user.email`, which is a strict, case-sensitive match that can diverge from other parts of the system if they normalize emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on the guests array in schema/UI, allowing unbounded inserts and email fan-out

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `addGuests` mutation whose input schema has `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`). The UI component `MultiEmail` allows arbitrarily adding more email fields via `updatedValue.push("")` with no limit (`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`). The handler then performs `createMany` inserts for all provided guests and triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails across attendees/team members (`addGuests.handler.ts`, `email-manager.ts`). This is a verifiable unbounded input leading to potentially unbounded DB inserts and email sending.

adjudication_records.issue_text: newGuests.includes inside a .map is O(n·m) and relies on a third independent email canonicalization point, fragile to future normalization at insert

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), the code does `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` and inside each iteration calls `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, which is O(attendees * newGuests) and could be replaced with a `Set` lookup. Also, the membership check is a strict string compare; the diff shows no canonicalization/normalization (e.g., lowercasing) of `newGuests` vs `attendee.email`, so future changes to how emails are stored/normalized could make this check brittle and affect which template is sent. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/perf concern, but not a clear functional defect by itself given typical small guest lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires caller to be BOTH admin and owner (&& instead of ||), narrowing the permission model and blocking team admins who are not owners
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && requires the user to be both team admin and owner, whereas the intended check should allow either role (use ||).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email logic uses raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so already-attending or blacklisted emails receive duplicate 'scheduled' confirmation emails with a fresh ICS
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: the function determines which attendees get which email by iterating over the full attendees list but uses the raw input guests/newGuests array (instead of the deduped/normalized set like uniqueGuests) for the `includes(attendee.email)` check, leading to wrong classification and duplicate/incorrect emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking status or time allows guests to be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, updating calendar attendees and sending confirmed ICS for nonexistent events

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts) authorizes by role but does not check any booking lifecycle constraints (e.g., `booking.status`, cancellation/rejection flags, or whether `booking.startTime` is in the past) before mutating attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sending ICS-based emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which hardcodes ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` in the new email templates. From the diff alone, guests can be added and "confirmed" updates sent for bookings regardless of status/time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New undocumented env var BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS silently drops guests from uniqueGuests without user-visible feedback or opt-in

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, a new env var `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is introduced and used to filter out emails when computing `uniqueGuests` (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Any blacklisted entries are simply omitted from `createMany` without returning which ones were rejected. If at least one non-blacklisted email remains, the mutation succeeds and the UI shows a generic success toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`), so blacklisted guests are dropped with no user-visible feedback. (Only the all-filtered case throws `BAD_REQUEST`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer and team members receive new_guests_added notification emails even when zero guests were actually added, and emails don't list which guests triggered them, making notifications unactionable

adjudication.rationale: The diff prevents sending when no *new* guests are added: `uniqueGuests` is computed and if `uniqueGuests.length === 0` it throws `TRPCError(BAD_REQUEST)` before emails are sent (addGuests.handler.ts). So the “zero guests were actually added” part is not supported by the diff. However, the notification templates don’t include which guests were added: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`/`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` don’t accept or render a guest list, and only set a generic title/subject (`new_guests_added`, `guests_added_event_type_subject`), making the emails less actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist filter case-normalization mismatch: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but compared against raw guest, allowing bypass with mixed-case emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares it against the raw `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (or otherwise case-normalized), a blacklisted address like `test@example.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Test@Example.com` (valid per `z.string().email()`). This is a real, diff-verifiable blacklist bypass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate attendee check 'guest === attendee.email' is case-sensitive, allowing same email in different case to be re-added creating duplicate rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicate prevention uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since `guest` comes directly from input (`z.string().email()` does not normalize case) and stored attendee emails may differ by casing, the same email can be re-added with different case, creating duplicate attendee rows. Relatedly, blacklist checking lowercases only the blacklist entries, not `guest`, so case variants could bypass the blacklist as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization predicate uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring user to be both admin and owner so team admins get FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore deny access to team admins who are not also owners, contradicting the intent implied by the variable name and the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No limit (.max()) on number of guests per request, allowing thousands of emails in one mutation

adjudication.rationale: The new mutation input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (and the client-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` is also unbounded). This means a caller can submit an arbitrarily large array of emails in one `viewer.bookings.addGuests` request, potentially causing excessive DB writes (`createMany`) and downstream work (calendar attendee update + sending emails), which is a verifiable robustness/security defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rate limiting on the addGuests mutation, enabling spam/email-forgery amplification sent from the organizer's identity

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` authed mutation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx` + `addGuests.handler.ts`) can be invoked by any authorized attendee/organizer/team admin/owner and triggers outbound email sending via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with no throttling/cooldown logic shown in the handler or router. That creates a concrete abuse/spam risk tied to this change, but the diff alone cannot confirm there isn’t global API rate limiting/middleware elsewhere, and the “email-forgery from the organizer’s identity” aspect is somewhat overstated (the organizer email is mainly used as `replyTo`; `from` is the app mailer address in organizer emails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee (guest) can add arbitrary further guests to someone else's booking with no organizer confirmation or privilege check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization gate explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the mutation proceeds unless `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. There is no further confirmation/approval step before `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, so an attendee on a booking can add arbitrary additional attendee emails to that booking via the API (even if the UI were later restricted). The finding’s phrasing about “no privilege check” is slightly off (there is a check), but the core issue—attendees being permitted to add more guests without organizer confirmation—is verifiable in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest-added attendees receive full booking details including videoCallData.url and password

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `CalendarEvent evt` built for the updated booking includes `videoCallData` with `url` and `password` when a video reference exists, and this same `evt` is used for both `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, newly added guest emails (those whose `attendee.email` is in `newGuests`) are sent an `AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)`, which would typically include the full event payload (including video call info). This is a real, diff-grounded privacy/security consideration, but whether it's a defect depends on product intent (added guests arguably need join details).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error handling swallows email-send failures with console.log not logging err, while reporting success 'Guests added' even when notifications failed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email notification step is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows failures and does not log `err`. The handler then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI shows a success toast on mutation success, so notification failures are not surfaced even though the core mutation (adding attendees) succeeded. This is a concrete observability/error-reporting concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a functional defect if the intended behavior is to not block guest addition on email failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Overly broad trpc error message rendered to client in onError with raw tRPC error message

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds a toast message using `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx). This directly surfaces the server-provided tRPC error `message` (and code) to end users; if any thrown error contains non-i18n/internal text, it would be shown verbatim (or as an untranslated key), which is an information disclosure / overly broad error exposure introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx error branch showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error") can never show the fallback since message is a template literal that is at minimum ': '

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the error handler builds `message` as a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always yields a string (at minimum `"undefined: "` or `": "`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback. This can lead to displaying an unhelpful/ugly error like `"undefined: ..."` instead of the intended generic message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); } swallows email-send failures silently and returns { message: "Guests added" } regardless

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which intentionally swallows any failure and still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. The diff confirms this behavior. It’s not necessarily a functional defect because guests are already persisted and calendar attendees updated before the email step, but it is a real, diff-grounded issue: failures are not surfaced to the caller and the error is only logged without the exception details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendee rows written non-atomically with calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts:105-112 — no rollback, compensating delete, or transaction; failure after guest insert leaves committed guests never invited to calendar, and user retry creates duplicates

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). There is no Prisma transaction covering both the DB write and the external calendar update, and no compensating rollback if updateCalendarAttendees throws. That means a failure after the DB update can leave guests committed in the database but not reflected in the calendar/invites, while the API call fails. Also, because a retry re-reads attendees and filters them out, uniqueGuests can become empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST, blocking a straightforward retry to re-run the calendar update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No removal endpoint exists for guest rows — once written, guests can only be removed via manual DB surgery, making the feature's writes effectively irreversible

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new write path that persists additional attendees (server: `addGuestsHandler` does `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})`), plus UI to trigger it (`AddGuestsDialog` -> `trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests`). Within this diff, there is no corresponding UI or TRPC mutation/handler/schema to remove guests once added, so guest additions created by this feature are not directly reversible via the newly introduced API/UI. However, the finding’s absolute claim that no removal endpoint exists anywhere in the codebase can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests persisted with name: "" in addGuests.handler.ts:90-98 and no backfill/update path — downstream emails, calendar invites, and ICS files permanently render nameless guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guest attendees are created with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails` mapping) and persisted via `attendees.createMany`. The diff shows no subsequent update/backfill path to populate names, and downstream payloads reuse `attendee.name` (e.g., `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, and email templates address recipients as `${name} <${email}>`). This is a real, diff-grounded data/UX concern (names will remain empty and may surface in emails/invites), but it's not clearly a correctness defect since the feature only collects emails and may intentionally not have names.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts:51-53, making the team-admin-or-owner branch dead code — only users who are both admin and owner pass; team admins get FORBIDDEN for organizer-less bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner. The variable name and subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`) indicate it is intended to allow either role; as written, a team admin who is not also owner will fail and hit `FORBIDDEN` even though they should be permitted for team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedup and blacklist comparisons in addGuests.handler.ts:82-86 are case-sensitive for attendee emails but case-insensitive for the blacklist, allowing near-duplicate guest rows (e.g. Bob@example.com vs bob@example.com) and blacklist bypass

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (via `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`, so a differently-cased email can bypass the blacklist. Also, dedup against existing attendees uses `guest === attendee.email` without case normalization, allowing near-duplicate rows like `Bob@example.com` vs `bob@example.com` to pass `uniqueGuests` and be inserted via `createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests handler silently drops duplicate/blacklisted guest emails while returning success message, with no indication of which emails were skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by dropping emails already present on the booking and any `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). If some are dropped but at least one remains, it proceeds to update and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` without reporting which inputs were skipped. This is verifiable from the diff and can mislead callers into thinking all submitted emails were added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending failure is silently swallowed in catch block with error discarded and success shown to user despite guests not receiving notifications

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, failures from `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` are caught and only `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` is executed, with the error details discarded and the handler still returning `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means the client mutation `onSuccess` will still show `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` even if notification emails were not sent. However, the primary operation (adding attendees + updating calendar attendees) still completes, so this is more of an observability/UX concern than a strict correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Promise.all in sendAddGuestsEmails means one failed email rejects the batch and remaining emails are silently abandoned

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the code builds an array of send promises and then `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. With `Promise.all`, any single rejection will reject the whole await early, so the function won’t wait for the rest of the email sends to finish. In `addGuests.handler.ts` this call is wrapped in a broad try/catch that only logs, so a single send failure can cause the batch to be treated as failed/unfinished even if other sends could succeed (an `allSettled`/per-email error handling approach would be more robust).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are committed to DB before external calendar update with no rollback on failure, leaving permanent DB state desynced from calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards the external calendar is updated with `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. If the calendar update throws, there is no surrounding transaction/rollback or compensating action, so the new attendees remain persisted while the external calendar may not be updated (desync). The subsequent email sending is wrapped in try/catch, but the calendar update is not, reinforcing the partial-update risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Subsequent retry after calendar failure hits duplicate filter and errors with emails_must_be_unique_valid, making failure unrecoverable from UI

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the DB is updated first (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany) and only afterward the calendar is updated (await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)) without a try/catch or rollback. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails but the guests are already persisted. A subsequent retry with the same emails will be filtered out by `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... !booking.attendees.some(...))`, resulting in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and a BAD_REQUEST error `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, preventing the user from retrying to fix the calendar sync from the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners fail the authorization check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) { throw FORBIDDEN }` will therefore deny access to team admins who are not owners (and not the organizer/attendee), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email dedup comparison in addGuests handler allows duplicate attendee rows for same person with different email casing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication uses a case-sensitive comparison (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`), while inputs are not normalized to a consistent casing (schema is `z.string().email()` only). This allows adding the same email with different casing (e.g., `User@x.com` vs `user@x.com`) and `createMany` will insert a duplicate attendee row. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` is also case-sensitive (`new Set(emails)`), so it won’t prevent this either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema dedup in AddGuestsDialog is also case-sensitive, accepting ['A@x.com','a@x.com'] as unique

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the client-side dedup/validation uses `new Set(emails)` inside `refine`, which compares strings case-sensitively. This means inputs like `["A@x.com", "a@x.com"]` will be treated as unique and pass validation. The server schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` also does not normalize/dedup, so this can result in duplicate attendee records differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: guests array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no .max() cap, allowing unbounded DB writes and outbound email volume per request

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (no `.max(...)`). The handler then uses `createMany` with `guestsFullDetails` and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fan-outs emails based on attendees/new guests. This makes it possible for a single request to trigger arbitrarily large DB writes and outbound email volume (resource exhaustion/DoS risk), directly grounded in the added schema and handler.
